sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Scleral buckling is an extra-ocular surgical procedure for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD). It involves the application of a buckle (silicone explant) to the sclera, creating an indentation to relieve vitreous traction and seal the retinal break by closing the gap between the RPE and neurosensory retina.

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Step-by-Step
content: 2. Muscle Isolation: Secure 4 recti muscles with 2-0 silk sutures.
3. Localization: Indirect ophthalmoscopy to mark retinal break.
4. Cryotherapy: Apply trans-scleral cryopexy around the break to create chorioretinal adhesion.
5. Explant Placement: Suture silicone sponge or solid element to the sclera.
6. Drainage: Optional external subretinal fluid drainage via sclerotomy (if bullous).
7. Closure: Secure buckle, tighten encircling band (usually #40 or #240).

content.explanation: C: Check the break localization; R: Relief of traction; Y: Yielding high attachment (cryo); O: Observe for post-op IOP spikes.

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Goldmann three-mirror exam for peripheral break localization.
Indirect Ophthalmoscopy with 20D lens is the gold standard.
Scleral indentation reveals the break-buckle relationship.
Pre-op B-scan USG is mandatory in dense cataract to assess detachment extent.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always check the buckle height: it should be at least 2 disc diameters wide to cover the break.
Avoid over-tightening the encircling element to prevent anterior segment ischemia.
Prophylactic drainage of subretinal fluid is controversial; reserve for bullous detachments.
Post-operative myopic shift is expected; warn patients of change in refraction.
